result.title: SecureGARD: Dynamic Ontology-Guided Governance for Secure Tool-Using LLM Agents
result.summary: Tool-using large language model (LLM) agents translate model outputs into consequential actions, turning indirect prompt injection into an execution-security problem. Existing defenses constrain tool calls, trajectories, or information flows, but often leave action semantics, state dependencies, and evidence relations implicit, limiting generalization across heterogeneous tools and complicating safe updates. We present \ours{}, a dynamic ontology-guided governance framework. \ours{} grounds heterogeneous calls in a shared semantic representation and combines an executable ontology with episode-level task state to derive deterministic ready, waiting, and forbidden decisions. A waiting decision identifies an unmet but recoverable obligation, enabling bounded replanning without expanding the agent's authorization boundary. \ours{} evolves its ontology offline from verified training executions. An offline LLM proposes instance-independent action--state axioms, which are accepted only if they address ontology errors exposed by training failures, preserve logical consistency and protected entailments, and pass held-out validation before the ontology is frozen. We evaluate \ours{} on AgentDojo, ASB, and AgentDyn under benign and indirect prompt-injection settings. \ours{} achieves a 0\% attack success rate (ASR) across all three benchmarks while improving task utility under attack compared with existing baselines. These results show that explicit semantic governance can strengthen execution security without indiscriminate blocking.

AI.brief_summary: 该文提出 SecureGARD，用可执行本体结合 episode 级任务状态，把工具调用归入统一语义表示并给出 ready／waiting／forbidden 的确定性决策，本体则从经过验证的执行轨迹离线演化，在 AgentDojo 等基准的间接提示注入设置下评测安全性。
AI.relevance_reason: 其显式任务状态、未满足义务与「继续／等待／禁止」判定，可能与 LVR 中基于证据充分性和状态依赖的停止决策及动作门控形成类比线索，但无视觉或多模态推理内容，需核查这种状态判定的实际形式是否可借用。
